name: Henry's Farm Adventures (Zumorroda-X)
tagline: A story-driven farming game: travel with Henry to farmers facing floods, heat, drought and salty soil, and solve each with real NASA satellite data.
problem: How farmers adapt to heat waves, floods, drought and salinization — and how satellite data reveals those risks — is hard for students and non-experts to grasp.
solution: A Phaser web game in which a struggling farmer travels to India (2021 heat), Pakistan (2022 floods), Egypt (salinization), the United States (drought) and Brazil (crop management); each stop turns NASA data — heat maps, Landsat before-and-after imagery, NDVI, the U.S. Drought Monitor — into a mini-game, plus a small model that predicts crop survival from CO₂ levels and adaptation choices.
demo_moment: Team-described: sliding between NASA satellite images of Pakistan before and after the 2022 floods, then placing straw and drainage pipes to save the fields.

why_it_stood_out.claim: Won the award for the project that most effectively combines technical and creative skills.
Puts the player in a farmer's shoes on a world journey, so adapting to climate hazards is experienced rather than read.
Every level is anchored in a real place and event (India's 2021 heat, Pakistan's 2022 floods) with the matching NASA imagery.
States its own limits (some hazards, such as wildfires, are not covered), which reads as honest scope.
The game framing turns an agriculture-data challenge into empathy plus learning, which works for judges who are not agronomists.

lessons: Let the user play the stakeholder; empathy is a judging advantage.
Anchor each scene in a real place, date and dataset.
When an award rewards art and technology together, staff both on purpose.

sources.note: Team-written game design, levels, data sources, tools and AI-use disclosure.
